Wider Sports News.title: FSG cashes in but what next for Liverpool after Bezos consortium’s UK£1.65bn deal?
Wider Sports News.summary: Liverpool have achieved huge on and off-field success under Fenway Sports Group and it now feels the time is right to reap the rewards. But will new minority shareholders seek more revenues or control and will FSG sell up? The post FSG cashes in but what next for Liverpool after Bezos consortium’s UK£1.65bn deal? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
A consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has agreed to buy almost a third of Premier League giants Liverpool from Fenway Sports Group (FSG) in a deal that values the club at a reported UK£5.5 billion (US$7.45 billion).

The 1892 Holdings consortium, the name of which refers to the year the Merseyside club were founded, will acquire a 30 per cent stake worth UK£1.65 billion (US$2.24 billion) and will have the option to take full control should FSG decide to sell in the future.

Wider Sports News.title: GSE Worldwide launches GSE advisory, names Michael Brown executive vice president
Wider Sports News.summary: New advisory practice builds upon GSE's existing brand services to help organisations maximise their investment in sports. The post GSE Worldwide launches GSE advisory, names Michael Brown executive vice president appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
New York (July 28, 2026) – GSE Worldwide (GSE), a leader in sports and entertainment marketing, event production and talent management, today announced the launch of GSE Advisory, a new advisory practice that expands the company’s existing brand-facing capabilities by providing senior-level strategic guidance to brands, rights holders, investors and sports organizations navigating growth through sports. The company also announced the appointment of industry veteran Michael Brown as executive vice president, GSE Advisory, effective July 27.

Building upon GSE’s existing brand services, the launch of GSE Advisory marks the next phase in GSE’s continued evolution, adding a dedicated advisory practice to the company’s existing capabilities across talent representation, experiential marketing, hospitality, and live events. By combining strategic guidance with direct access to the people, platforms, and experiences that shape today’s sports landscape, GSE Advisory will help brands answer critical questions around where to invest, which partnerships create the greatest value, and how to maximize their investments in sports.

Wider Sports News.title: What the LA Lakers’ sunning quickfire US$12.5bn sale says about the state of US sports investment
Wider Sports News.summary: Less than 12 months after being officially confirmed as the owner of the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers, Mark Walter is ready to sell to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner. The billionaire’s shock exit is set to generate a remarkable short-term profit – and a lot of questions. The post What the LA Lakers’ sunning quickfire US$12.5bn sale says about the state of US sports investment appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
For the second time in two years, the Los Angeles Lakers are about to become the most expensive team in world sport. Pending approval from the league board, the 17-time National Basketball Association (NBA) champions will sell for a reported US$12.5 billion to a group led by former Disney chief executive Bob Iger and Josh Kushner – venture capitalist, younger brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, and recent associate of Fifa president Gianni Infantino.

It is an extraordinary development. The deal comes less than a year after current owner Mark Walter was cleared to take the franchise out of the hands of the Buss family, when his purchase of a controlling stake valued the Lakers at US$10 billion.

Wider Sports News.title: Formula E turns to Disney+ to reach new audiences through global streaming deal
Wider Sports News.summary: All-electric series will balance global deal with existing FTA and pay TV rights in respective markets. The post Formula E turns to Disney+ to reach new audiences through global streaming deal appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Formula E is prioritising reach over exclusivity through its new global streaming deal with Disney+, according to the series’ chief media officer Michaella Snoeck. The multi-year agreement, which officially gets underway from the start of the 2026/27 season, will cover 144 territories around the world and sit alongside the all-electric series’ existing portfolio of free-to-air (FTA) and linear broadcast partners.

“This is not just the global home, we have multiple partners in multiple markets,” Snoeck told SportsPro. “It is a much broader and wider ecosystem and want to obviously reach as many fans as possible. So there’s always going to be a blend of either free-to-air or pay [TV] in each respective market.”

Wider Sports News.body:
The National Football League’s (NFL) domestic broadcast deals are the envy of almost every rights holder on the planet. Back in 2021, it guaranteed its status as sport’s richest league for another decade. A new set of broadcast contracts – running from the 2023 season until 2033 – secured US$111 billion from CBS, Fox, NBC, ESPN and Amazon.

Further deals for one-off matchups, the Sunday Ticket package of out-of-market matchups, and a global partnership for select set-piece games with Netflix, including Christmas Day, have increased this revenue stream even further.

Wider Sports News.title: Pools revealed for rugby sevens at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
Wider Sports News.summary: Pools revealed for rugby sevens at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games HSBC SVNS Series
Wider Sports News.body:
Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time when some of the world’s most promising young players take to the field at Dakar 2026. The Opening Ceremony is on 31 October and the rugby tournament kicks off at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop the following day, with medals awarded on 2 and 3 November. Dakar 2026 is set to make history as the first Olympic sporting event to be staged on the African continent. Around 2,700 young athletes are expected to compete across 25 competition sports.

Eight men’s and eight women’s rugby sevens teams have qualified for Dakar 2026, with the competitions featuring two pools of four teams. Australia, China, Kenya and hosts Senegal will compete in Pool A, while Pool B features Czechia, Madagascar, Spain and USA.

Wider Sports News.title: Why Birmingham Phoenix chose strategy over cash in the Hundred’s franchise sell-off
Wider Sports News.summary: The 2026 season marks the first time the impact of the Hundred’s new team owners has been clearly visible across the ECB’s 100-ball cricket competition. While some franchises have traded elements of their identity for investment, Warwickshire CEO Stuart Cain explains why Birmingham’s brand and long-term interests were always non-negotiable. The post Why Birmingham Phoenix chose strategy over cash in the Hundred’s franchise sell-off appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The sixth edition of the Hundred is by far and away the most significant campaign of the 100-ball franchise cricket competition since it debuted five years ago. The 2026 season is the first since the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) permitted outside investment into its eight constituent franchises, a process which has raised UK£500 million that will be used to shore up the grassroots and county game.

Investors include some of the biggest technology companies in the world, private equity firms, and the backers of Indian Premier League (IPL) teams. The off-season has been marked by rebranding exercises, greater outlays on playing staff, and a shift from centralised governance that has put more power into the hands of individual franchises, including the ability to secure their own sponsorship agreements.

Rugby.title: Wallabies boosted as three outside backs likely to be fit for Argentina
Rugby.summary: Les Kiss will continue to test the limits of his Wallabies unit in Argentina, adamant its more flexible than even the players think.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss will continue to test the limits of his Wallabies unit in Argentina, adamant its more flexible than even the players think. A squad for the two-Test tour – their first game is in San Salvador on August 29 – is likely to be named on Wednesday.

It’s understood Max Jorgensen, who limped off with sore ribs after a collision in the side’s big Townsville win over Japan on Saturday, will be fit to travel. Centres Len Ikitau (ankle) and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii (hamstring) are also firming for returns, giving their coach more welcome headaches after casting the net wide in his first two games in charge.

Rugby.title: Three-time World Cup player returning home for Super Rugby Pacific
Rugby.summary: The offload specialist has made 132 professional appearances across stints at the Glasgow Warriors, Racing 92, Toulon and Castres, and won 68 Test caps.
Rugby.body:
Three-time World Cup player Leone Nakarawa is returning home to Fiji to play for the Drua in the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific competition. One of the most storied Flying Fijians of all time, Nakarawa is set to bring much-needed experience to the young Drua squad.

As well as being a part of three Rugby World Cup campaigns, including 2015 when he was selected in the official team of the tournament, the 38-year-old was part of their gold medal-winning sevens squad at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

Rugby.title: Hansen forced to draft in two players ahead of ‘pressure’ Wallaroos clash
Rugby.summary: Following the Black Ferns' clash with the Wallaroos, they will travel to South Africa to feature in a double header with the All Blacks in Johannesburg on September 5.
Rugby.body:
Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has been forced to draft in two Black Ferns XV players ahead of their clash with the Wallaroos at Mt Smart Stadium on Saturday evening. The Black Ferns, who beat the Black Ferns XV 62-19 in Upper Hutt last Friday, will take on Australia in Auckland on Saturday to kick-start a busy international period for Hansen’s side.

The Wallaroos will head into the contest without their newly appointed head coach, as Sione Fukofuka is only taking the reins from January 2027. But for Hansen and the Black Ferns, the original squad has changed following the trial match, with both Tara Turner and Mo’omo’oga Palu picking up injuries that have made them unavailable for the weekend.

Rugby.title: Josh Moorby reveals All Blacks’ expectations of Boks amid style debate
Rugby.summary: There's been a tense feel to the first Test week in the Republic, with both coaches responding to and discussing certain narratives surrounding this weekend's showdown at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks outside back Josh Moorby isn’t feeding into the narratives around the Springboks possibly slowing the game down ahead of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour. There’s been a tense feel to the first Test week in the Republic, with both coaches responding to and discussing certain narratives surrounding this weekend’s showdown at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.

The All Blacks, who have preached a fast-paced contest, are clear in their intentions to take the game to the Springboks from the get-go in the first Test. One player who will welcome the All Blacks’ high ball-in-play attitude is Moorby, who dotted down for two tries against the Bulls in Pretoria, continuing his exceptional try-scoring form from the 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season.

Rugby.summary: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus and technical consultant Jaco Peyper have responded to the narrative that the Springboks want to play a 'slow game' against the All Blacks.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus and technical consultant Jaco Peyper have responded to the narrative that the Springboks want to play a ‘slow game’ against the All Blacks.

Peyper revealed that “not once” have the Springboks got feedback that they slow the game down in 2026 following the new protocols for feedback. The former referee who now consults to the Springboks confirmed the law that the Springboks play to, which is that they have 30 seconds from the time the mark is given to form the set piece.

Tuipulotu could be labelled an experienced campaigner in the Republic, compared with others in the All Blacks’ touring squad who may never have played in South Africa or against the Springboks before the tour.

Rugby.title: Jason Ryan’s blunt assessment of the Springboks’ scrum ahead of first Test
Rugby.summary: "I think we took a step forward tonight [against the Bulls], I really do," Ryan told Justin Marshall on Sky Sport.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Jason Ryan has given Rassie Erasmus and the Springboks all of the credit ahead of the first Test in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, labelling their scrum “the best in the world”.

Ryan, who has now travelled to South Africa under head coaches Ian Foster, Scott Robertson, and now Dave Rennie, will be preparing his forward pack for one of rugby’s biggest challenges at Ellis Park in Johannesburg this weekend.

Rugby.title: Five women’s rugby internationals who have represented two nations
Rugby.summary: This weekend Pia Tapsell could become the first rugby player to have represented both the Black Ferns and Wallaroos.
Rugby.body:
This weekend Pia Tapsell could become the first rugby player to have represented both the Black Ferns and Wallaroos. When the two teams meet at Mount Smart Stadium for the second Laurie O’Reilly Cup clash of 2026, Tapsell may make her Wallaroos debut against the Black Ferns, for whom she made six appearances between 2019 and 2020.

Born in Melbourne, but raised in New Zealand from the age of eight, the loose forward has switched allegiances after two seasons with the Western Force in Super Rugby Women’s and has described her international recall as a “fresh start”.

Rugby.title: Three-time Champions Cup winner joins coaching staff of Élite 1 hopefuls
Rugby.summary: Toulon legend Jocelino Suta has joined the coaching staff of Toulon ahead of the 2026/27 AXA Élite 1 Féminine season.
Rugby.body:
Toulon legend Jocelino Suta has joined the coaching staff of Rugby Club Toulon Provence Méditerranée ahead of the 2026/27 AXA Élite 1 Féminine season. Across a 13-year playing career the Vanuatu-born enforcer made 233 appearances for Toulon across a decade at the club, won three Champions Cup titles and earned six caps for France.

Suta came off the bench in the 2013 and 2014 Champions Cup Final successes against Clermont and Saracens, as a squad containing the likes of Jonny Wilkinson, Bakkies Botha, Matt Giteau and Carl Hayman dominated continental club rugby. In 2015, Suta made seven tournament appearances as the club claimed a third title in a row.

Rugby.summary: Scarlets Director of Rugby Nigel Davies admits that Wales centre Eddie James signing a new deal is significant for the club, who are battling the Ospreys for the WRU West Wales licence.
Rugby.body:
Scarlets Director of Rugby Nigel Davies admits that Wales centre Eddie James signing a new deal is significant for the club, who are battling the Ospreys for the WRU West Wales licence.

Rugby.summary: Is New Zealand's 'Greatest Rivalry' tour of world champions South Africa a signpost to the future of rugby union?

Wales centre Eddie James has signed a new contract with Scarlets. After making his international debut in 2024, James became a Wales regular in the 2025-26 season under head coach Steve Tandy and now has 11 caps to his name.

Rugby.title: How the Springbok Women reacted after 'proper Test match' against Fiji
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women assistant coach Franzel September said it was "mission accomplished" for the team after their completed a Test series whitewash against the Fijiana XV.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women assistant coach Franzel September said it was “mission accomplished” for the team after their completed a Test series whitewash against the Fijiana XV. A week after South Africa had beaten Fiji 55-12 in Suva, the Boks battled their way to a 29-22 victory in Lautoka to wrap up the nation’s first-ever tour of Fiji with walkover success after two fixtures.

“We wanted a clean sweep, so that was mission accomplished,” September said. “We expected Fiji to come back stronger in the second test after winning 55-12 in the first and they did. This was a proper Test match.”

Rugby.title: Dual international Willis Halaholo announces retirement
Rugby.summary: Former Wales and Tonga centre Willis Halaholo has announced his retirement at the age of 36.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales and Tonga centre Willis Halaholo has announced his retirement at the age of 36. The nine-cap Wales international made the announcement on social media on Monday, sharing a video in which he said he plans to move into coaching.

The Auckland-born centre made the move to Cardiff from the Hurricanes in 2016, and qualified to play for Wales in 2019. After initially being named in a Wales squad in 2019, an ACL injury meant he would have to wait until 2021 before he would play international rugby.

Rugby.summary: Red Roses head coach John Mitchell has called Daisy Hibbert-Jones and Sophie McQueen into the team's University of Nottingham training camp.
Rugby.body:
Red Roses head coach John Mitchell has called Daisy Hibbert-Jones and Sophie McQueen into the team’s University of Nottingham training camp. The Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 are entering the third week of their WXV Global Series preparations. In September and October, England will play Canada three times, as well as the Black Ferns, Wallaroos and USA Women’s Eagles.

Hibbert-Jones, 23, earned one cap for England at WXV 1 in 2023 as the Red Roses claimed the inaugural title in New Zealand. Last season the back-row captained Loughborough Lightning in JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby to a sixth-place finish in the league.

All Blacks 2IC Neil Barnes isn’t satisfied with his team’s efforts to begin the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, despite an accumulated 142-40 scoreline through three games against their club opponents.

Rugby.title: Ex-Wales and Cardiff centre Halaholo retires
Rugby.summary: Former Wales and Cardiff centre Willis Halaholo has ended his professional rugby career after 'a series of niggling injuries'.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales and Cardiff centre Willis Halaholo has ended his professional rugby career. The 36-year-old announced his retirement on social media, saying "the mind is still keen to carry on but I think the body has had enough".

Auckland-born Halaholo qualified for Wales under residency rules and won the last of his nine Wales caps in April 2022. He went on to play three times for Tonga. He began his career in New Zealand with Southland before spells with both Waikato and Hurricanes, where he won a Super Rugby title.

Rugby.summary: Despite Tapsell playing rugby in New Zealand since she was eight years old, the Western Force forward was born in Melbourne.
Rugby.body:
Pia Tapsell has no qualms about being in the Wallaroos squad, despite growing up in New Zealand and playing Test rugby for Australia’s bitter rivals. Tapsell became one of the few women’s international rugby union players to switch allegiances after she named in the Australian squad to face the Black Ferns in Auckland on Saturday.

It’s the first time the Wallaroos have experienced a player swap from a tier-one nation, although the Wallabies notably had prop Alex Hodgman play for the green and gold in 2024 after switching from the All Blacks.

Rugby.summary: Kadin and his brother Treyvon have been at the centre of contract speculation following their breakout seasons with the Brumbies and Queensland Reds respectively.
Rugby.body:
Kadin Pritchard admits it was an easy decision to re-sign with the ACT Brumbies and stay in rugby union until the end of 2030, despite receiving a sparkling offer to join PNG Chiefs.

Kadin and his brother Treyvon have been at the centre of contract speculation following their breakout seasons with the Brumbies and Queensland Reds respectively. They attracted headlines when the incoming NRL club approached the pair looking to poach them for their inaugural roster in 2028, which risked dealing a blow to Rugby Australia as they look primed for a future Wallabies debut.

Rugby.summary: Isaac Henry's display against Japan proved that other brands - other than Joseph-Aukuso Sua’ali’i - are available for the Wallabies' No.13 jersey.
Rugby.body:
The UK broadcasting rules are strict. When presenters on a telly show inadvertently mention a prominent commercial product on air, it is considered to be free advertising. The culprit is required to qualify the gaff with the prompt disclaimer ‘other brands are available, of course’. Usually, with a hint of a smirk curling around the corners of the mouth.

Rugby.summary: Sir Steve Hansen has weighed in on the All Blacks' decision to bring Richie Mo'unga into camp as a replacement for Billy Proctor, who has headed home after picking up a shoulder injury.
Rugby.body:
Sir Steve Hansen has weighed in on the All Blacks‘ decision to bring Richie Mo’unga into camp as a replacement for Billy Proctor, who has headed home after picking up a shoulder injury.

The ex-New Zealand head coach, who selected Mo’unga at No.10 during the 2019 Rugby World Cup, commended the current group, led by Dave Rennie, for not rushing the decision to find Proctor’s replacement, saying the time taken to assess their options builds confidence that they have made the right choice.

Rugby.title: The four top performers from round three of the Hilux NPC
Rugby.summary: The third round of the NPC saw some landmark records established and new contenders emerge.
Rugby.body:
The third round of the NPC saw some landmark records established and new contenders emerge. Hawke’s Bay stayed on top of the table with a 44-31 win over Auckland. Flanker Cooper Flanders from the 2019 Hastings Boys’ High School National Top Four-winning First XV has been a slow burn, but with two tries and 16 tackles, he has carried on his strong recent form and looks more settled and confident. Can he soar to the heights of his brother Devan Flanders?

Otago required late heroics from All Black Christian Lio-Willie and All Blacks XV winger Jona Nareki to quell Manawatu 29-27 after trailing 24-7. There was a similarly stoic comeback from Southland to upset Waikato 32-31 in Invercargill. In just his third appearance, 19-year-old Jimmy “The Boot” Taylor landed a sideline conversion with the last kick of the game to win it for the Stags.

Rugby.summary: Looking back, Blair was pleased with the overall performance against the Bulls, but also believed they could have been more clinical.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Mike Blair has described his side’s attacking progress as a “mixed bag” to date, despite winning all six contests under Dave Rennie in 2026. Blair assumed the attack role at the start of the 2026 international season, joining the coaching staff of Rennie, Neil Barnes, Tana Umaga, and Jason Ryan.

The experienced Scotland halfback, speaking to media in Pretoria, was asked how he feels the attack is progressing after the three encounters against South African URC sides. Looking back, Blair was pleased with the overall performance against the Bulls, but also believed they could have been more clinical.

Rugby.summary: Former Springboks head coach Heyneke Meyer believes that the gulf in depth between the two sides will be the difference in the Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Former Springboks head coach Heyneke Meyer believes that the gulf in depth between the two sides will be the difference in the Greatest Rivalry series. According to the ex-coach the All Blacks don’t have the numbers in the forwards to match the Boks, while the game has changed to suit South Africa.

The eligibility rules in New Zealand have meant that a number of players head offshore when their international careers aren’t progressing, leading to a lot of departures in their late 20s.

Rugby.title: Predicted All Blacks' 23 to face the Springboks in the first Test
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks will name their team to face the Springboks on Thursday, with a number of players uncertain after injuries across the first three warm-up games.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks will name their team to face the Springboks on Thursday, with a number of players uncertain after injuries across the first three warm-up games. Prop Ollie Norris is the latest to be sent home after succumbing to an injury, while Cortez Ratima joins the uncertain list with a knee complaint.

Centre Billy Proctor, winger Caleb Clarke, hooker George Bell are all ruled out of further participation and have been sent home. In doubt includes Will Jordan (back complaint), Cam Roigard (hamstring), Damian McKenzie (ankle), and Ratima, with McKenzie the most worrying of the injuries according to head coach Dave Rennie.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.summary: The return of RIchie Mo'unga has long been anticipated and he will soon get the chance to show Dave Rennie what he can do
Rugby.body:
A bit like the Mounties, it was always the case that Dave Rennie was going to get his man and bring Richie Mo’unga into the All Blacks. Everyone knew this was inevitable – that the All Blacks were almost certainly going to see someone suffer a tour-ending injury in South Africa and that Mo’unga would be deemed the right replacement by Rennie almost regardless of who was heading home.

As it turned out, it was midfielder Billy Proctor who cracked his shoulder in the opening game and Rennie was able to persuade the New Zealand Rugby board of directors that Mo’unga, a specialist No 10, was the player he needed to call-up.

Rugby.title: WRU statement: 'Highly personal insults and attacks' directed at staff
Rugby.summary: The WRU have decried what they have described as'highly personal insults and attacks' directed at their staff and members of the board in recent weeks.
Rugby.body:
The WRU have decried what they have described as’highly personal insults and attacks’ directed at their staff and members of the board in recent weeks. In what amounts to more of a open letter to the Welsh rugby public than a traditional statement, the WRU have asked fans to desist from attacks directed at their personal.

The statement reads: “Whatever your views about what is best for the future of Welsh rugby, there is no justification for the highly personal insults and attacks that have been recently directed at members of our staff and at the WRU Board.

Rugby.summary: Without knowing that was happening across the ditch, Wallaby Taniela Tupou did all front-rowers proud on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
TOWNSVILLE: New Zealand’s NPC celebrated ‘Front Row Round’ this week, recognising the hookers and props who have contributed to provincial rugby over 50 years. Without knowing that was happening across the ditch, Wallaby Taniela Tupou did all front-rowers proud on Saturday.

Tupou hadn’t scored in consecutive games since April 2021, when the world-renowned tighthead was suiting up for the Queensland Reds. The now 72-Test prop rewrote the script with a memorable double on Saturday, playing a leading role in a 56-17 win over Japan.

Rugby.summary: Stand-in All Blacks captain Codie Taylor, who scored a double in his first appearance on tour, said that he feels as though his side has made considerable strides during these tour outings.
Rugby.body:
Despite the All Blacks securing three wins from three games so far on Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, head coach Dave Rennie is keeping his feet firmly on the ground. His side put 50 points on the 2026 United Rugby Championship runners-up, the Bulls, 54 on the Sharks, and 38 on the Stormers, charging to six wins on the trot ahead of the four-Test series.

But Rennie is clear that they are far from the perfect product, and will need a shift in quality if they want to secure a famous victory at Ellis Park next weekend. Touching on the contest post-match in Pretoria, the All Blacks head coach said the scoreline is a positive, but there were still aspects of the game that were “frustrating”.

Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have beaten the Bulls by 50-19 in Pretoria to remain undefeated on the Greatest Rivalry tour. Outstanding performances from Anton Segner, wingers Josh Moorby and Leroy Carter and Josh Jacomb fuelled a high-tempo All Blacks team that looked the sharpest it has so far on the tour.

The All Blacks survived an early onslaught from the home side, repelling multiple mauls from the five before a statement scrum which put the Bulls pack on the floor. After coming up inches short of the line, the Bulls were given a scrum five out which the All Blacks won a penalty against the feed.

Rugby.title: USA Rugby adopts T1 as official non-contact game ahead of home World Cups
Rugby.summary: USA Rugby and USA Youth & High School Rugby have formally adopted T1 Rugby as the official non-contact version of the game in the United States...
Rugby.body:
USA Rugby and USA Youth & High School Rugby have formally adopted T1 Rugby as the official non-contact version of the game in the United States, in a move designed to boost participation ahead of the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups on American soil in 2031 and 2033.

Developed by World Rugby and launched in 2023, T1 replaces tackling with touches or flags while retaining rugby’s core principles. Played seven-a-side on a half-pitch, the format is aimed at schools, clubs and youth organisations as an accessible entry point into the sport.

Rugby.summary: Ospreys are set to announce former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones as a new member of their board before the 2026-27 season.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones is poised to return to the Ospreys as a director. The 40-year-old is set to be announced as a board member by the Swansea-based club next week.

Jones made his Ospreys debut in 2005, a year after he broke through with Swansea RFC, and helped the club to three titles and an Anglo-Welsh Cup triumph. The former lock is to return at a turbulent time as the club fights for survival under Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans to cut to three professional men's sides.

The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has stated there is no realistic prospect of the game generating enough revenue to fund four professional teams in the country beyond 2028. The WRU's board has released a lengthy statement after former Wales captain Jonathan Davies called for them to step down.

There has been a concerted attempt to try to oust the WRU board this week. Businesswoman Hayley Parsons called for them to stand down before Davies' intervention, while former Principality Building Society chief operating officer Rob Regan has offered to oversee an interim board.

Rugby.body:

A former radio station employee felt he could not tell anyone he was being indecently assaulted by Alan Jones because of the talkback titan’s extraordinary power and influence.

He is one of six men who allege Jones kissed, groped or subjected them to sexual misconduct between 2003 and 2020 across Sydney and the NSW Southern Highlands. The 85-year-old has pleaded not guilty to 22 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching without consent.

Rugby.title: Rugby Sevens set for historic return at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Rugby Sevens set for historic return at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games EWN
Rugby.body:
Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time when the world's best young players compete at Dakar 2026 in Senegal. The tournament will kick off on November 1 at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop, just one day after the opening ceremony on October 31. Medals will be awarded on November 2 and 3.

Dakar 2026 will make history as the first Olympic sporting event ever held on the African continent. The games will bring together around 2,700 young athletes competing across 25 different sports, including athletics, boxing, 3x3 basketball and coastal rowing.

Mano had been rewarded for a series of impressive Major League Rugby campaigns with the Utah Warriors, earning higher honours with appearances against Brazil and Spain. But the now 31-year-old hasn’t played at the international level since.

Rugby.title: Rieko Ioane opens up on questioning whether his All Blacks career was over
Rugby.summary: Few All Blacks careers capture the hype, awe and contention of Rieko Ioane's. In July, a decade after becoming the eighth-youngest All Black ever in his 2016 debut, he was dropped from the squad for the first time
Rugby.body:
Few All Blacks careers capture the hype, awe and contention of Rieko Ioane’s. In July, a decade after becoming the eighth-youngest All Black ever in his 2016 debut, he was dropped from the squad for the first time. The now 29-year-old has since been recalled in an expanded squad for the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, and has opened up on thinking his All Blacks days were done.

Sitting on 40 career Test tries, the eighth-most in All Blacks history, Ioane’s elite finishing was a constant feature of the team in his early years, although that strike rate dropped off considerably with his 2020 move to the midfield.

Rugby.title: Davies calls for WRU board to step down
Rugby.summary: Former Wales captain Jonathan Davies calls for the Welsh Rugby Union board to step down.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales captain Jonathan Davies has called for the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) board to step down. Calls for the governing body's board to resign have come from Welsh business leaders while local Swansea politicians have demanded that chief executive Abi Tierney leave her role.

There are 11 members on the board following the departure of chair Richard Collier-Keywood in March 2026. Tierney is joined by interim vice-chair John Manders, independent directors Jamie Roberts, Jennifer Mathias, Andrew Williams, Alison Thorne and Amanda Bennett, elected members Claire Donovan, Chris Jones and Colin Wilks and interim Professional Rugby Board (PRB) chair Marianne Okland.

Rugby.title: Start of England's community rugby season postponed
Rugby.summary: The Rugby Football Union delays the start of the community rugby season because of concerns about player welfare and pitch conditions affecting much of England.
Rugby.body:
The Rugby Football Union has delayed the start of the community rugby season because of concerns about player welfare and pitch conditions affecting much of England. According to officials, 71.3% of England is now in drought while the country has recorded its driest July since records began in 1836.

In recent weeks, the RFU has reminded its members of existing guidance on managing rugby pitches in drought conditions and carrying out risk assessments to see if pitches are safe to use and to mitigate the risks of injury.

NBA superstar San Antonio Spurs forward-centre Victor Wembanyama has spent this week training with Pro D2 promotion hopefuls Provence Rugby at the Maurice-David Stadium. Wembanyama, 22, who hails from Le Chesnay in the western suburbs of Paris, was the first pick in the 2023 NBA draft and is a two-time NBA All-Star, and spent the week taking part in several drills during on-field training sessions with Philippe Saint-André’s squad.

He was part of the France squad that won an Olympic silver medal at the Paris Games, but there is very little prospect of the 7 ft 4 in star ever switching codes after signing a five-year £186m extension with the Spurs last month.

Rugby.title: 57-cap prop returns to centrally contracted Ireland group for 2026/27
Rugby.summary: Experienced Ireland prop Linda Djougang has rejoined the union's centrally contracted programme for the 2026/27 season.
Rugby.body:
Experienced Ireland prop Linda Djougang has rejoined the union’s centrally contracted programme for the 2026/27 season. Last year the 57-cap front-row stepped away from the full-time programme to pursue her career outside of rugby, but remained a player of national interest and started all five Guinness Women’s Six Nations fixtures in 2026.

Sophie Barrett, Kate Jordan, Aoibheann McGrath and Eilís Cahill – who all made their Test debuts at this year’s Championship – have all earned their first national contracts. This centralised group of 31 players has been announced three months after Scott Bemand’s side enjoyed a record-breaking Women’s Six Nations campaign. This included a crowd of 31,294 at the team’s first standalone fixture at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium.

Rugby.title: Shifting sands in the game
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks will play the Bulls who have, in coach Kennedy Tsimba, a visionary who has evolved the game in South Africa
Rugby.body:
In the Shona language native to Zimbabwe there is a well-known phrase: ‘tsimba itsoka’. It means ‘no foot, no footprint’ and it refers firstly to the footprint an animal may leave on the veld; on the larger scale of human activity, it highlights to the deep mark a man or a woman may leave on the ground of life.

A few weeks ago, I met Kennedy Tsimba, the current Skills coach of the Pretoria-based Bulls. As a player, Kennedy was a star in Sevens and he was anointed the ‘King of Bloemfontein’ for his record-breaking try-scoring feats with the Cheetahs. Tsimba became the fastest player to score over 1000 points in the Currie Cup, the Vodacom Cup and Super Rugby during his six-year stint in the Vrystaat and he is remembered. The footprint is strong.

Rugby.body:
Ben Gunter was two grades above me at Brisbane Boys’ College. In my five years at the school, no First XV debut seemed to generate more anticipation than when Gunter first took the field as a 15-year-old, starring alongside future Wallaby Isaac Henry that season.

Rugby.title: New All Blacks Sevens coach reveals stance on XVs stars chasing Olympics
Rugby.summary: Willie Rickards played in eight tournaments for the All Blacks Sevens from 2006 to 2009. He succeeds Tomasi Cama.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks Sevens have a new head coach. Willie Rickards played in eight tournaments for the All Blacks Sevens from 2006 to 2009. He succeeds Tomasi Cama, who was involved with the 14-time SVNS Series champions for two decades and 150 tournaments as a player and coach.

Rickards represented Southland (28 games), Taranaki (19 games) and the Highlanders (2 games) as a player before moving into coaching. He led the Taranaki Sevens programme to a National Championship in 2013 and was NPC Skills Coach during the 2014 NPC Premiership-winning campaign. He then progressed to Assistant Coach and Head Coach (2018-2020). His tenure included a notable Ranfurly Shield win over Canterbury, 55-43 in Christchurch in 2017. However, the overall record as head coach was a modest 12 wins in 33 matches.

Rugby.title: Debutants star for Black Ferns in big win over Black Ferns XV
Rugby.summary: A special exhibition match took place in Upper Hutt on Friday afternoon, with the Black Ferns locking horns with the Black Ferns XV in a high-scoring encounter.
Rugby.body:
A special exhibition match took place in Upper Hutt on Friday afternoon, with the Black Ferns locking horns with the Black Ferns XV in a high-scoring encounter. It was a game for the debutants to reward the selectors for their faith, and Elinor-Plum King, Amarante Sititi and Shyrah Tuliau-Tua’a all validated their inclusions in the top squad, with King claiming three tries in the 62-19 win.

Sititi won a breakdown penalty for the Black Ferns on the halfway line in the second minute, with Ruahei Demant’s kick to touch giving her team an early chance to attack from just outside the 22. Sititi and Demant featured again in the ensuing phase play with touches that furthered momentum, ultimately contributing to a try in the corner for Mererangi Pual.

Rugby.title: Bay of Plenty sniff history: 'Times might have changed, the Shield hasn’t'
Rugby.summary: Bay of Plenty has a sorry Ranfurly Shield record with only two wins in 25 matches stretching back more than a century.
Rugby.body:
Bay of Plenty has a sorry Ranfurly Shield record with only two wins in 25 matches stretching back more than a century. The only successful challenge the Steamers have mounted for the Log o’ Wood was on August 15, 2004. Glen Jackson scored in all four ways, bagging 23 points as the challengers stunned defending NPC champions Auckland 33-28 in the opening round of the 2004 season at Eden Park.

On Saturday, 22 years to the day after that success, Bay of Plenty will challenge NPC champions Canterbury for the Ranfurly Shield at Te Kaha, One New Zealand Stadium. Canterbury won the Shield from Otago 19-15 in Dunedin on Sunday. Bay of Plenty, after a shocking 38-26 loss to start the 2026 NPC in Hamilton where they were down 35-0 at halftime, edged past Northland 34-31 in Rotorua last weekend.

On Saturday, 22 years to the day after that success, Bay of Plenty will challenge NPC champions Canterbury for the Ranfurly Shield at Te Kaha, One New Zealand Stadium. Canterbury won the Shield from Otago 19-15 in Dunedin on Sunday. Bay of Plenty, after a shocking 38-26 loss to start the 2026 NPC in Hamilton where they were down 35-0 at halftime, edged past Northland 34-31 in Rotorua last weekend.

Rugby.summary: Marno Redelinghuys will be back in the red, white and blue this weekend, named at blinside flanker for the USA XV.
Rugby.body:
Marno Redelinghuys will be back in the red, white and blue this weekend, and USA XV captain Jason Damm didn’t hold back when expressing his excitement over the selection – describing the South African-born backrower as both “a dog” and “a beast.”

It’s been more than 270 days since Redelinghuys last represented the USA at the highest level, suiting up at lock in a 26-18 win over Romania in November. The 33-year-old followed that up with 10 appearances for the Seattle Seawolves during the 2026 Major League Rugby season.

Rugby.title: Arrivals and exits: A country-by-country look at the Top 14's new signings
Rugby.summary: We stand on the doorstep of another exhilarating and fiercely contested Top 14 season, making it the perfect time to take a deep dive into the foreign legion players set to leave their mark on French rugby's premier competition.
Rugby.body:
We stand on the doorstep of another exhilarating and fiercely contested Top 14 season, making it the perfect time to take a deep dive into the foreign legion players set to leave their mark on French rugby’s premier competition.

From the 24 nations set to participate in next year’s World Cup, only three won’t have any personnel featuring in the Top 14: Zimbabwe, Canada and Hong Kong China Rugby. There was a slight uptick from one season to the other, as the foreign legion considered for this article went from 214 to 224 players. Portugal went from zero to three representatives with the arrivals of captain José Madeira, flanker Nicolás Martins, and prolific try-scorer Rodrigo Marta.

Rugby.title: 2029 auditions and unpredictability: John Mitchell sets England's sights on the WXV Global Series
Rugby.summary: A John Mitchell press conference 30 days out from the Red Roses' first WXV Global Series fixture of 2026 felt akin to the first assembly of a new school year.
Rugby.body:
A John Mitchell press conference 30 days out from the Red Roses’ first WXV Global Series fixture of 2026 felt akin to the first assembly of a new school year. Players roam the various halls at the University of Nottingham wearing their new team kit. There have been several new faces in camp. A few new lessons being taught. It really is the start of something new. And that is just about where the ‘back to school’ analogy ends.

The Red Roses will arrive into the WXV Global Series riding the ever-growing wave of their 38-match unbeaten streak. It was only in May that Mitchell’s side secured a fifth Guinness Women’s Six Nations Grand Slam in a row. Soon enough it will be one year since their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 triumph over Canada in front of a world record crowd at Allianz Stadium. Things are very much business as usual.

Rugby.summary: While international coaches seem to think solely in terms of World Cup cycles in modern rugby, Rassie Erasmus has taught the world in recent years that it is never too late to burst onto the Test scene.
Rugby.body:
While international coaches seem to think solely in terms of World Cup cycles in modern rugby, Rassie Erasmus has taught the world in recent years that it is never too late to burst onto the Test scene.

Of his 2019 world-beating Springboks side, Cheslin Kolbe, Makazole Mapimpi, RG Snyman and Kwagga Smith were all uncapped in 2018. Likewise, Kurt-Lee Arendse, Deon Fourie, Grant Williams and Manie Libbok got their first taste of Test rugby in 2022 before lifting the Webb Ellis Cup in 2023.

Rugby.title: 'I shouldn't be wasting it': Why Nomsa Mokwai balances rugby with full-time nursing
Rugby.summary: Nomsa Mokwai is currently taking unpaid leave from her job as an emergency room nurse to play for South Africa in a two-Test series in Fiji.
Rugby.body:
Nomsa Mokwai is currently taking unpaid leave from her job as an emergency room nurse to play for South Africa in a two-Test series in Fiji. Mokwai, who starred in the Springboks’ 55-12 win over Fiji last Saturday and will start again this weekend, is used to juggling her full-time job with rugby.

She works 12-hour shifts, usually at night, as a nurse before carrying out her rugby training in the day. It is a lot to balance but the 33-year-old sees playing rugby as a gift.

Rugby.summary: The Scarlets have bolstered their front row options ahead of the 2026-2027 United Rugby Championship campaign by signing Moana Pasifika tight-head Chris Apoua.
Rugby.body:
The Scarlets have bolstered their front row options ahead of the 2026-2027 United Rugby Championship campaign by signing Moana Pasifika tight-head Chris Apoua. Auckland-born Apoua, 34, who has Samoan heritage, has scored one try in seven appearances for Moana Pasifika and has played for Northland and Southland at provincial level in New Zealand, making his debut a decade ago.

He is Scarlets Director of Rugby Nigel Davies’ eighth signing this summer and joins Wales loosehead Corey Domachowski, who moved from Cardiff when his contract ran out at the end of June.

Rugby.summary: Premiership champions Northampton Saints appoint Fraser Dingwall as their new club captain.
Rugby.body:
English Prem champions Northampton Saints have appointed Fraser Dingwall as their new club captain. The 27-year-old centre steps into the role after George Furbank's move to Harlequins.

Dingwall, who joined Saints' academy aged 13, has made more than 150 senior appearances and becomes the club's 69th captain since its formation in 1880. "When you look at the list of players who've done it before, it's incredibly special to be part of that group," said the England international, who has won 10 caps since his Test debut in 2024.

Dingwall has been a key figure at Franklin’s Gardens since making his senior debut in 2018, having joined the Saints academy at the age of 13. He has since made more than 150 appearances for the club and has already captained the side on several occasions.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has named his matchday 23 to face the Bulls in the final fixture before next weekend’s series-opener against the Springboks. The new starting XV features two starting debuts, one in the No.1 jersey for Xavier Numia and one in the No.10 jersey for Josh Jacomb. The Chiefs pivot’s selection comes as Beauden Barrett shifts to fullback, a position he hasn’t played for the All Blacks since he was last in South Africa in 2024.

There’s positive injury news to be found in the front row, too, with acting tour captain Codie Taylor and Tyrel Lomax both overcoming their setbacks to start in what is sure to be a hard-fought set piece battle.

Rugby.summary: It’s incredible to think that Tuesday only marks ten years to the day since Fiji’s famous victory.
Rugby.body:
While the Rio 2016 winners of the women’s tournament, Australia, can be regarded as one of the most significant teams in the history of the short format, there is one team that serves as a worthy challenger to their legacy: the men’s gold winner from that very same Olympics.

It’s incredible to think that Tuesday only marks ten years to the day since Fiji’s famous victory: because it’s a victory that already feels well-etched into the history of rugby.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.summary: The injection of Tim Walsh and Reg Tayler into the Wallaroo coaching set up has proven a massive positive for Maddison Levi.
Rugby.body:
The injection of Tim Walsh and Reg Tayler into the Wallaroo coaching set up has proven a massive positive for Maddison Levi, the sevens speedster keen to bring her skillset to XVs after being named in the squad that will travel to New Zealand to face the Black Ferns.

The Wallaroos’ match at Mount Smart Stadium in Auckland will mark their 100th Test match and their 45th in just five years, and that elusive maiden victory over the Black Ferns still awaits from 30 attempts.

Rugby.summary: Johan Ackermann has named four South Africa internationals in his starting Bulls XV to take on the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Johan Ackermann has named four South Africa internationals in his starting Bulls XV to take on the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday. The Bulls boss promised “we’re going to go as strong as we can” this week despite missing a large swathe of players in Rassie Erasmus’s squad, and he has remained true to his word, naming several regular Bulls players alongside the Springboks.

Former Bok Marcell Coetzee will captain the side, and will be joined by 101-cap Springbok Willie le Roux, and Embrose Papier, who earned his first Bok cap in eight years when he started against Scotland in July. Papier will form a half-back partnership with fellow Bok Curwin Bosch, who will mark his return to South Africa after two years in France with Brive.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga receives long-awaited All Blacks call-up
Rugby.summary: Richie Mo'unga is en route to South Africa to join the All Blacks squad ahead of their game against the Bulls in Pretoria this weekend.
Rugby.body:
Richie Mo’unga is en route to South Africa to join the All Blacks squad ahead of their game against the Bulls in Pretoria this weekend. The 32-year-old is three years removed from his last All Blacks cap, which came in New Zealand’s 2023 Rugby World Cup final defeat to the Springboks, having surrendered his All Blacks eligibility when signing with Toshiba Brave Lupus in Japan Rugby League One.

Having now completed that contract and signed with Canterbury, the Crusaders and New Zealand Rugby on an 18-month deal, Mo’unga’s eligibility for national selection was reinstated with his first minutes in the NPC two weeks ago, and will remain until his contract expires after next year’s Rugby World Cup.

Rugby.body:
Yes, two games into their tour to South Africa, the performances have been pretty good. I’m not sure they’ve been pushed too hard by their opponents or we’ve learnt much that we didn’t already know, but there’s definitely not a lot to complain about.

Rugby.title: Canterbury's latest Ranfurly Shield hero describes chaotic Otago win
Rugby.summary: Dominic Gardiner wrote himself into Ranfurly Shield folklore in Canterbury’s successful 19-15 challenge against Otago at Forsyth Barr Stadium in Dunedin on Sunday.
Rugby.body:
Dominic Gardiner wrote himself into Ranfurly Shield folklore in Canterbury’s successful 19-15 challenge against Otago at Forsyth Barr Stadium in Dunedin on Sunday. In the last minute, hard-pressed on defence, Gardiner ripped the ball off Otago replacement hooker Nic Souchon at a ruck. This turnover allowed Canterbury to keep possession until the clock stopped.

“Those turnovers are split-second decisions,” Gardiner told RugbyPass. “I noticed Nic was slightly isolated so I made a grab for the ball, got a cling on it and ripped it away.

Rugby.summary: Saracens' England 'A' centre Angus Hall signs a new contract with the Prem club.
Rugby.body:
Saracens' England 'A' centre Angus Hall has signed a new contract with the Prem club. The 20-year-old, who came through the club's academy, made three Prem appearances last season as well as playing once in the European Champions Cup and three times in the Prem Rugby Cup.

He also spent time on loan at Champ side Ampthill as well as featuring against Spain and an All Blacks XV for England's 'A' side in November. "Angus is exactly the type of player we want to build this club around," newly-appointed director of rugby Brendan Venter told the Saracens website.

Rugby.title: Steve Borthwick makes 5 changes to his 2025/26 Elite Player Squad
Rugby.summary: England have revealed the 25 players who will receive enhanced Elite Player Squad contracts ahead of the new season, with five changes made in total.
Rugby.body:
England have revealed the 25 players who will receive enhanced Elite Player Squad contracts ahead of the new season, with five changes made in total. The five new additions are Gloucester centre Seb Atkinson, Northampton Saints lock Alex Coles, Sale Sharks prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, Bath flanker Guy Pepper and Leicester Tigers scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet.

These new additions are not exactly like-for-like replacements for the five players who have lost their contracts. While Pepper can be seen as a direct replacement for Ben Curry, who failed to play a game for England last season due to a recurring hamstring issue, as can Atkinson for Ollie Lawrence, who fell out of favour during the Six Nations, the final three changes are not like-for-like.

Rugby.title: 'Say ‘yes’ and figure it out afterwards': How one decision changed Jane Clohessy's life
Rugby.summary: Back in November 2022, not long after Jane Clohessy got off stage with her band, a message arrived on her phone.
Rugby.body:
Back in November 2022, not long after Jane Clohessy got off stage with her band, a message arrived on her phone. It was from former Ireland captain, Niamh Briggs – ‘Any interest coming to a Munster session?’

It was not an immediate ‘yes’ but, from that moment, Clohessy’s life would set off down a different path. The Limerick native hails from a rugby-mad family. Her father is Munster and Ireland legend, Peter Clohessy. Many childhood years were spent in and around stadiums and clubhouses. Born in December 1998, Clohessy would have been too young to clearly recall her dad, ‘The Claw’, chasing down Heineken Cup and Six Nations glory. What remains is that feeling of being embraced by a wider family.

Rugby.title: Five players get first England deals in Borthwick shake-up
Rugby.summary: Asher Opoku-Fordjour, Alex Coles, Guy Pepper, Jack van Poortvliet and Seb Atkinson are handed England central contracts for the first time as Steve Borthwick shakes up his squad.
Rugby.body:
England boss Steve Borthwick has shaken up his centrally contracted squad with just over a year to go until the Rugby World Cup. Borthwick has announced the 25 players who will receive enhanced player contracts, worth around £150,000, for the 2026-27 season.

Handed an elite deal for the first time are prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, lock Alex Coles, flanker Guy Pepper, scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet and centre Seb Atkinson. Flanker Ben Curry, versatile back Elliot Daly, centre Ollie Lawrence and wing Tom Roebuck all miss out on contracts, while France-bound number eight Tom Willis is no longer eligible for England selection.

Rugby.title: Ospreys say WRU plan to cut team is wrong
Rugby.summary: Ospreys respond publicly to WRU plans for the first time with the belief four professional Welsh sides is the way forward.
Rugby.body:
The Ospreys board has told the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) its plan to reduce a professional side is the wrong decision. Welsh rugby's governing body has outlined its plans to cut the number of professional teams from four to three by 2028, with WRU-owned Cardiff and privately-backed Dragons set to be given licences.

That announcement has plunged Scarlets and Ospreys into doubt, with the west licence either being awarded to the Llanelli-based side or their Swansea-based rivals. WRU chiefs have said the process to decide the framework for the final decision will begin in December and finish before the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

Rugby.summary: England's Red Roses are in pre-season training before the upcoming WXV Global Series and have been using the controversial smaller balls.
Rugby.body:
England's women are in Nottingham for pre-season this month before the upcoming WXV Global Series. In the new competition, the Red Roses will take on Australia, Canada and New Zealand on home soil in September before further tests across the Atlantic against Canada again and the USA in October.

The last time we saw the world champions in action they were winning another Six Nations' Grand Slam - so what's new? Head coach John Mitchell spills the beans. World Rugby's new size 4.5 balls - about 3% smaller but the same weight as a regulation size five - will be used for the WXV Global Series and are now in use in the England camp.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: One thing Les Kiss will like about his first Wallabies win
Rugby.summary: The new Australia head coach started his tenure with a win, but several areas require improvement before they face Japan again.
Rugby.body:
A new Wallabies era under a new head coach has finally begun, and even if it wasn’t overly convincing, at least it started with a win. Australia’s 35-32 victory over Japan was a whole lot more free-flowing and open in steamy Osaka than their 19-15 win in cold, wet Tokyo last season, but the contest left us in the odd situation where both teams will head into Saturday’s return leg in Townsville with a good degree of confidence.

The first encounter was an entertaining game to watch, frustratingly so at times for Wallabies fans, and it really sets up a mouth-watering contest this weekend. While Les Kiss and his coaching team will take positives from the three-point win, there were also more than a few things that need some urgent attention this week.

Rugby.title: Nonu performs solo haka in response to All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks star Ma'a Nonu responds to the haka by performing one of his own before his club side's game with New Zealanders in Durban.
Rugby.body:
New Zealand rugby union great Ma'a Nonu performed a solo haka in response to the All Blacks' haka before his Sharks side fell to a heavy defeat in Durban. The All Blacks continued their tour of South Africa with a resounding 54-0 victory, though what happened pre-match will go down in rugby folklore.

After New Zealand performed their usual Ka Mate haka, Nonu stepped in front of his Sharks team-mates and responded with Kapa o Pango, the All Blacks' alternative haka. The 44-year-old played 104 matches for New Zealand between 2003 and 2015, and was part of the side that won the Rugby World Cup in 2011 and 2015.

Rugby.summary: Former England assistant coach Brian Smith has died at the 59 after a battle with an aggressive cancer.
Rugby.body:
Former England assistant coach Brian Smith has died at the 59 after a battle with an aggressive cancer. Dr Ian PM Lambert, principal Scots College where Smith had worked since 2015, confirmed his death on Wednesday.

The former fly-half made six appearances for Australia, including three at the 1987 Rugby World Cup, before earning nine caps for Ireland while studying at Oxford University. Upon his return to Australia, Smith made the move to rugby league, where he made 43 NRL appearances across four seasons for the Balmain Tigers and Eastern Suburbs.

Rugby.title: 10 years on: Remembering Fiji’s historic gold at Rio Olympics
Rugby.summary: It’s been 10 years since one of the most famous days in rugby sevens history, when Fiji defeated Great Britain 43-7 to win Olympic gold.
Rugby.body:
It’s been 10 years since one of the most famous days in rugby sevens history, when Fiji defeated Great Britain 43-7 to win Olympic gold in Rio. The 2016 Rio Summer Games marked the return of rugby union to the Olympic stage, and the first time sevens had been on show.

Rugby had been held at the Olympics four times before, with the USA going back-to-back with gold medals in 1920 and 1924, and France collected silver on those two occasions. But the sport didn’t return to the Olympics, in any format, for more than 90 years.

Rugby.title: Ethan de Groot makes 'easy' call on future with new deal until 2029
Rugby.summary: The deal's announcement comes just hours after De Groot suited up for a non-Test match against the Sharks in Durban, playing 54 minutes in the 54-0 win.
Rugby.body:
Ethan de Groot has re-committed his future to New Zealand Rugby, the Highlanders and Southland until 2029. The move will ensure the loosehead prop’s eligibility at the time of the next British and Irish Lions Tour of New Zealand, with the opportunity to add to his 43-Test tally in the meantime, including at next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia.

The deal’s announcement comes just hours after De Groot suited up for a non-Test match against the Sharks in Durban, playing 54 minutes in the 54-0 win. He cited the arrival of his first child, Nova, as a major reason to stick around, even though overseas offers were undoubtedly on the table.

Rugby.title: Seven clips the Wallabies will be analysing after another tight win over Japan
Rugby.summary: Let’s be blunt: seven linebreaks is far too many, and so is the total of nine the Japanese managed to get against the Wallabies, according to the stats.
Rugby.body:
Let’s be blunt: seven linebreaks is far too many, and so is the total of nine the Japanese managed to get against the Wallabies, according to the stats. It was the first look at new defence coach Scott McLeod’s defensive system, and it was every bit as aggressive as head coach Les Kiss had foreshadowed during the week, saying he wanted to “attack” with defence.

While nine linebreaks were recorded, seven of them will likely feature heavily in review this week for the Wallabies. It will be embarrassing watching for some, frustrating for others, with varying degrees of complexity in solving the issues.

Rugby.summary: Aseza Hele had a long wait between her 32nd and 33rd Test caps for the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Aseza Hele had a long wait between her 32nd and 33rd Test caps for the Springbok Women. Before last weekend’s 55-12 win over the Fijiana XV in Suva, the last time the back-row wore a green and gold jersey was in the team’s quarter-final exit against the Black Ferns at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

A hand injury that required surgery meant that Hele missed out on a chunk of the Pick n Pay Women’s Super League 1 campaign and the two Test series against the USA Women’s Eagles in July.

Rugby.title: Ulster reveal summer surgery to Henderson alongside three team-mates
Rugby.summary: Ulster have confirmed that captain Iain Henderson will be out of action for a "number of months" after undergoing an operation on his hip this summer.
Rugby.body:
Ulster have confirmed that captain Iain Henderson will be out of action for a “number of months” after undergoing an operation on his hip this summer. While the procedure was a success, the 34-year-old will nevertheless be sidelined for the start of the season, which begins on September 25 for Ulster with a visit from Edinburgh in the United Rugby Championship.

The 85-cap international is one of four players who have gone under the knife during the offseason, with fellow Ireland representative Bryn Ward also part of that list. The 22-year-old made his debut for Andy Farrell’s side in July against Japan, but has since had his shoulder operated on.

Rugby.title: Experienced former Champ boss Williams joins Gloucester Hartpury as assistant
Rugby.summary: Cambridge's former Director of Rugby, Richie Williams, has joined JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby side Gloucester Hartpury as an assistant coach.
Rugby.body:
Cambridge’s former Director of Rugby, Richie Williams, has joined JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby side Gloucester Hartpury as an assistant coach. During a six year stay at Cambridge, Williams masterminded the club’s rise from National 1 to Champ Rugby in 2023. He left The Blood and Sand a year later.

Williams most recently was backs and attack coach of Champ club, Chinnor, with whom he spent almost a decade with as a player. Last term the Oxfordshire club placed fifth in the league and competed in a play-off quarter-final. Last year Williams also worked as an assistant for Oxford University.

Rugby.title: Why Rassie will be happier than Rennie with early omens of Greatest Rivalry tour
Rugby.summary: A stop-start, set-piece-based game like the Stormers tour opener will not suit the All Blacks if the pattern extends into the Test series.
Rugby.body:
The intensity is back, the novelty is back. The Greatest Rivalry in rugby is finally back on the rails. The novelty has been given a huge helping hand by South Africa’s abandonment of Super Rugby and move towards northern domestic competitions. The players no longer experience the ho-hum staleness of the over-familiar. The razor-edge intensity has been merely dormant, awaiting the time to wake up like a vengeful ghost summoned on some unwitting rugby Ouija board.

The 47,130 baying fans at the DHL Stadium in Cape Town will eagerly testify to both. It was a portentous occasion with meaningful bite, and in the course of the 80 minutes Springboks supremo Rassie Erasmus drew rather more blood than his counterpart Dave Rennie. The All Blacks beat the Stormers comfortably enough in the end, 38-21 and six tries to three, but the game was played out under rules which will suit South Africa rather more than New Zealand, if the early omens extend as far as the Test series which begins on 22 August at Ellis Park.

Rugby.title: Bath in 'serious discussions' to play in Reading
Rugby.summary: Reading owner Rob Couhig says the club have had "serious discussions" with Bath about the Prem Rugby club playing at their stadium.
Rugby.body:
Bath have had "serious discussions" about playing two of their 2026-27 games at Reading's Select Car Leasing Stadium, Royals owner Rob Couhig has said. Bath confirmed they will play their final two home games of the Prem season away from the Recreation Ground to enable construction work to begin as part of a redevelopment.

Couhig, who took over as Reading owner in May 2025, said the League One club have had talks with Bath but would not disclose how far they have progressed. "The stadium is well equipped for it, they would be foolish to not try and pursue us," the American told BBC Radio Berkshire.

South Africa’s first Test with the All Blacks gets underway in less than two weeks at Ellis Park, with no certainty as to who Erasmus will select at fly-half, or many other positions, for that matter, given the depth the world champions have across the field.

Rugby.title: 'The opportunity for growth is enormous': Fukofuka lands new coaching role after Scotland exit
Rugby.summary: Eight days after his exit as Scotland head coach Sione Fukofuka has been appointed head coach of the Wallaroos.
Rugby.body:
Eight days after his exit as Scotland head coach Sione Fukofuka has been appointed head coach of the Wallaroos. The 47-year-old left his role with Scotland after nearly eight months under compassionate grounds and cited ‘family stress’ as a reason for his departure from the position.

Across his five matches in charge of Scotland at the Guinness Women’s Six Nations, Fukofuka presided over one win against Wales at the beginning of the Championship. In addition to his tenure with Scotland, Fukofuka also spent time as head coach of the USA Women’s Eagles for two and a half years – who he led at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 – and spent three years as an assistant coach with the Wallaroos.

Rugby.summary: With Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 already far gone in the rear window mirror, the Yaras have, for the last two months, quietly adjusted and tweaked themselves ahead of the WXV Global Series Challenger.
Rugby.body:
With Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 already far gone in the rear window mirror, the Yaras have, for the last two months, quietly adjusted and tweaked themselves ahead of the WXV Global Series Challenger.

Now under the guidance of Guilherme Coghetto, recently appointed head coach of Brazil’s women’s national team, the Yaras are looking to the future, as he explains. “The 2025 World Cup will always be a wonderful moment in our history, but we need to look forward and keep growing. If we want to win a game in a World Cup, we need to be more competitive, and for that the team needs to increase its output, be it physical, technical and psychological.”

Rugby.title: 'The phoney war on the Greatest Rivalry tour is already gale-force in its intensity.'
Rugby.summary: A clash of styles is at the heart of The Greatest Rivalry and whoever prevails will set the tone for the short-term future of rugby
Rugby.body:
Are you sitting comfortably? Then I’ll begin with a story from a different era of rugby over 40 years ago, well before the advent of professionalism. A well-known, but highly-respected referee had just finished managing a Five Nations match between England and Ireland, in which he had kept the game flowing and penalized only the offences which were absolutely necessary.

At the dinner after the game, England captain and future World Rugby chair Bill Beaumont got up to speak: “I don’t normally do this… but I want to start by complimenting the referee for an exceptional performance. He was the best man on the field by far, and he deserved the man-of-the match award.” Cue a few guffaws from the suits. It was one of many pats on the back the official received after the game, from players and coaches alike.

Serena and Venus Williams lost a thriller at the Cincinnati Open in their first doubles match together for four years. The American pair were beaten 2-6 6-1 10-8 by Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in front of a packed crowd.

Tennis.title: Cincinnati Open: Britain's Arthur Fery loses despite thrilling fightback vs Alex de Minaur after rain delays
Tennis.summary: Cincinnati Open: Britain's Arthur Fery loses despite thrilling fightback vs Alex de Minaur after rain delays Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Britain's Arthur Fery was knocked out of the Cincinnati Open, but only after a thrilling fightback was halted by Alex de Minaur following several rain delays. In the end, fifth seed De Minaur ground out a 7-5 7-6 (7-3) win, but rain delays occurred before the contest, after the first game, following the end of the first set and with De Minaur 7-5 5-1 ahead, one game from the last-16 stage.

Yet, following the resumption Fery proceeded to rattle off five games in a row in a complete momentum shift, breaking De Minaur twice to move 6-5 ahead, only for the Australian to regain his composure and force a tiebreak.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu’s Ex-Coach Sends Strongly-Worded Message to Defend Rafael Jodar After Cincinnati Open Controversy
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu’s Ex-Coach Sends Strongly-Worded Message to Defend Rafael Jodar After Cincinnati Open Controversy Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu's former coach, Mark Petchey, came to Rafael Jodar's defense on Sunday after the Spaniard found himself at the center of controversy during the Cincinnati Open. The controversy erupted during the third set of Jodar's second-round match against Denis Shapovalov on Saturday. The Spaniard fought back from a 1-5 deficit and saved match points to win 7-5, 4-6, 7-5. During the deciding set, he stopped play twice, claiming that he had broken his shoelaces. The second incident came while he was trailing 3-5, forcing a lengthy pause as he completely changed his shoes.

Shapovalov grew visibly frustrated and complained to the chair umpire. He accused Jodar of using the shoelace delays not only to fix his equipment but also to disrupt his rhythm, get some rest, and drink water. The 19-year-old also faced backlash online, as he reportedly used similar tactics during his matches against Taylor Fritz at the Mubadala DC Open and Brandon Nakashima at the Canadian Open.

Tennis.title: Could Raducanu Retire Suddenly? Andrew Castle Says It Wouldn't Surprise Him
Tennis.summary: Could Raducanu Retire Suddenly? Andrew Castle Says It Wouldn't Surprise Him TennisTemple
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu is still sidelined after a stress fracture in her right leg, which notably forced her to withdraw from Wimbledon. The 2021 US Open champion is also expected to miss the North American hard-court swing after pulling out of the US Open. She was also not selected for the Billie Jean King Cup final with Great Britain at the end of September.

Faced with this succession of physical problems, former British player Andrew Castle believes that a radical decision from Raducanu would not be totally surprising. "Well, let's put it this way. I have absolutely no information about what's going on in her circle, but it wouldn't surprise me if one day, without warning, she simply says: 'I've had enough of all this.' After all, don't we all say that? She has no one to answer to but herself and her family. That's it. Sponsors and the people around her are not the ones driving this career. It's her choice, but I hope she continues," the former British tennis player told Betway.

The 39-year-old said the condition was exacerbated by the heat and humidity in Ohio as he visibly struggled in a 6-2 4-6 4-6 loss to Argentina's world No 50 Thiago Agustin Tirante.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu Handed Shock Retirement Warning by Ex-British No. 1 as Injury Forces US Open Absence

Tennis.body:
Former British World No. 1 Andrew Castle recently made a bold prediction about Emma Raducanu's career as she continues to recover from injury. Raducanu was last seen in action at the HSBC Championships, where she enjoyed a strong run and reached the final. However, she fell short of winning the title after losing to Donna Vekic in the final on June 14. Following the tournament, she has been away from the court due to a lower-leg injury sustained during the final.

After undergoing medical tests, the injury was diagnosed as a stress fracture in her right lower leg. The setback forced her to withdraw from Wimbledon just hours before her opening match. She has also pulled out of the Canadian Open and the US Open as she continues her recovery. The US Open is scheduled to take place from August 23 to September 13 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.

Tennis.body:
Britain's Arthur Fery beat Australia's James Duckworth at the Cincinnati Open, in his first match since making a shock run to the Wimbledon semi-finals last month. Fery, who jumped to a career-high world ranking of 36 following his Wimbledon success, won 6-4 2-6 7-6 (7-4) in two hours and 34 minutes against Duckworth in Ohio as he warms up for the US Open later this month.

The 24-year-old was given a wildcard into his home Grand Slam, having been ranked 114th in the world before the start of the tournament and having never been beyond the second round of a Grand Slam, and defied all expectations to reach the semi-finals where he lost to Alexander Zverev.

Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic suffered defeat and struggled physically in his first match since Wimbledon as he was upset by Thiago Agustin Tirante in a sapping three-set contest at the Cincinnati Open.

Djokovic, inactive on the ATP Tour since losing to Jannik Sinner at the grass-court Grand Slam on July 10, won the first set 6-2 but then lost the next two 6-4 as he battled the heat and humidity in Ohio, even appearing to vomit at one stage.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper: 'The Mountain Seems Huge' After Another Early Cincinnati Exit
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper: 'The Mountain Seems Huge' After Another Early Cincinnati Exit en.tennistemple.com
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper no longer really knows where he stands. At Cincinnati, the Brit once again left the tournament in his opening match, beaten by Martin Landaluce (6-3, 7-5). But beyond the result, it's especially the words of the 24-year-old player that are striking.

After several months marked by injuries, Draper now admits he increasingly struggles to find the player he once was. Long considered one of the future greats of the circuit, the former world No. 4 had a spectacular rise in 2025, notably with a title at Indian Wells and a final in Madrid.

Tennis.title: Ex-tennis player Bautista Agut scores on football debut
Tennis.summary: Roberto Bautista Agut scores twice on his debut for Spanish seventh-tier side CD Els Ibarsos - just over a month after retiring from tennis.
Tennis.body:
Just over a month after retiring from tennis, Roberto Bautista Agut has returned to competitive sport - this time on a football pitch. The 38-year-old former Wimbledon semi-finalist has signed for Spanish seventh-tier side CD Els Ibarsos and scored twice in a 4-2 win on his debut in a pre-season match.

The Spaniard's tennis career featured 12 singles title wins plus a Davis Cup triumph with his country in 2019. Achieving success on the football field is now his challenge. "It's a new stage of life that's making me very happy", Bautista Agut said on Instagram.

Tennis.title: Why I think Jack Draper should now skip the US Open after his first round loss at the Cincinnati Open
Tennis.summary: Why I think Jack Draper should now skip the US Open after his first round loss at the Cincinnati Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper lost again last night, meaning that of the last five tournaments he has entered, spanning five months, he has suffered four first-round exits. This is not nearly at the level we expect from the former world number four, but such a downturn is through no fault of his own.

Instead, this has been the cruel result of an injury he simply cannot fix, no matter what he tries. Rest has not resolved the bone bruising in his arm, and surgery would only make things worse. It’s the worst place for a professional athlete to be in, and it comes at a crucial time in Jack Draper’s career, just when he seemed set to be a mainstay at the apex for years to come.

Tennis.title: Swiatek beats Rybakina for first title of season
Tennis.summary: Iga Swiatek secures her first WTA title of the season with a straight-set victory over Elena Rybakina in the final of the Canadian Open.
Tennis.body:
Iga Swiatek secured her first WTA title of the season with a straight-set victory over Elena Rybakina in the final of the Canadian Open on Thursday. The six-time Grand Slam winner was cheered on by the crowd in Toronto as she beat world number two Rybakina 6-2 6-3.

Australian Open champion Rybakina struggled in the opening set and made 12 unforced errors, while Swiatek, 25, broke the Kazakhstan player's serve twice - and saved two breaks points of her own - to take the first set.

It proved another difficult day for the former US Open semi-finalist on his comeback from a longstanding bone bruising issue after he had broken down in tears during a defeat to Terence Atmane at last week’s National Bank Open in Montreal.
